title: Carnitine metabolism to trimethylamine by an unusual Rieske-type oxygenase from human microbiota
authors: Zhu Y, Jameson E, Crosatti M, Schäfer H, Rajakumar K, Bugg TD, et al.
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
population: Human Microbiome Project reference genomes; Acinetobacter baumannii ATCC 19606 mutants; recombinant Escherichia coli
funder: This work is supported by the Royal Society (RG2011/R1) and partially by the Natural Environment Research Council (NE/I027061/1).
authorConflicts: The authors declare no conflict of interest.
result: A two-component Rieske-type oxygenase/reductase, CntA and CntB, encoded in a carnitine utilisation gene cluster in 39 human microbiota reference genomes, cleaves the C-N bond of carnitine to trimethylamine and a four-carbon compound. Deletion of cntA or cntB abolished trimethylamine formation from carnitine in A. baumannii; purified CntA and CntB with NADH were necessary and sufficient in vitro. CntB is a predicted NAD(P)-dependent reductase with flavin and plant-type [2Fe-2S] ferredoxin domains; CntA carries a Rieske [2Fe-2S] centre and a mononuclear iron centre, and its glutamate 205 is essential for catalysis.
